question: All information from our environment is detected by the specialised tips of some nerve cells and these receptors are usually located in our sense organs such as:

options.text: the inner ear, the nose and the tongue

solution:
The correct answer is __**the inner ear, the nose and the tongue**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Our sense organs contain specialized receptors that detect information from the environment.
 
• The primary sense organs include the inner ear, nose, and tongue, which are equipped with different types of receptors.
 
• The inner ear contains mechanoreceptors that detect sound and balance.
 
• The nose contains olfactory receptors that detect smell.
 
• The tongue contains taste receptors that detect different tastes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Receptors**

 
 
• Receptors are specialized structures that respond to specific stimuli from the environment.
 
• Different receptors are found in various sense organs, each tuned to specific types of stimuli.
 
 
 
• **Mechanoreceptors**
 
 
• These receptors respond to mechanical stimuli such as touch, pressure, and sound.
 
• Found primarily in the skin and the inner ear.
 
 
 
• **Olfactory Receptors**
 
 
• These receptors are responsible for the sense of smell.
 
• Located in the nasal cavity and detect airborne chemicals.
 
 
 
• **Taste Receptors**
 
 
• These receptors detect different tastes such as sweet, sour, salty, bitter, and umami.
 
• Located on the taste buds of the tongue.
